organization: Example Organization (illustrative policy used for validation testing)
description: A sample set of organization-specific technical constraints, written to exercise the evaluator against the open-source test subjects. It does not represent the policy of any real organization.

rules.title: Projects must target a supported .NET release
rules.rationale: Releases outside this list no longer receive security fixes, so remaining on them carries unmitigated risk.

rules.title: Legacy data-access and web stacks are prohibited
rules.rationale: These packages are tied to .NET Framework and block migration to a supported runtime.

rules.title: Dependencies with published advisories must meet a minimum version
rules.rationale: Versions below these carry published security advisories.

rules.title: API projects must not depend on the legacy WCF stack
rules.rationale: Scoped rule: applies only to projects whose name identifies them as service APIs.

rules.title: Authentication must use OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect
rules.requirement: Confirm that the application authenticates through OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect rather than Forms Authentication.
rules.rationale: Cannot be decided from dependency and symbol analysis alone; an engineer must verify the configured authentication flow.

rules.title: Layered architecture boundaries must be respected
rules.rationale: Declared for a capability this version of the framework does not implement. It is reported as requiring human review rather than silently passing.
